hook: Two quantum observers can be certain they disagree, but only when their measurements do not commute.
hook_turn: but only when their measurements do not commute.
summary: The paper proves a quantum version of Aumann's Agreement Theorem: if the observers' measurements commute with each other and the property, common certainty forces equal probabilities. A qutrit-qubit-qubit model breaks this with common certainty of disagreement, and storing outcomes in a classical register restores agreement. The results are for finite-dimensional, projective-measurement setups.
title: The quantum agreement theorem.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
